questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-FwyQuk on main; one-time gstack setup prompt.
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules, so requests like "review this diff" route to the right skill automatically. This is a plain text section appended to CLAUDE.md.
Stakes if we pick wrong: without it you invoke skills by name manually; with it, plain requests auto-route. Either is reversible.
Recommendation: A because auto-routing removes a step from every future session and costs one commit.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: convenience now vs. one extra committed section in CLAUDE.md. Plan mode blocks file edits, so if you pick A the append + commit happens after this review exits plan mode.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Plain requests ("ship this", "find the bug") route to the right skill without naming it
✅ One short section, committed once; teammates get the same routing
❌ Adds a gstack-specific block to CLAUDE.md; applied after plan mode exits, not now

options.label: No thanks, manual invocation
options.description:
✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as it is; no tool-specific text in the repo
✅ You keep full control over when a skill runs
❌ Every skill needs its /name typed; re-enable later via gstack-config routing_declined false

questions.question:
D2 — Let gstack search learnings from your other projects on this machine?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-FwyQuk on main; one-time gstack setup prompt.
ELI10: gstack saves small lessons per project ("this test runner needs flag X"). Cross-project mode also searches lessons from your other local projects when reviewing this one. Everything stays on this machine.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too narrow and you miss patterns you already learned elsewhere; too broad and a client codebase could surface a lesson from another client's repo in a review.
Recommendation: A because this is a solo-style environment and the data never leaves the machine.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: more recall vs. strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Lessons from other local projects surface here when they match a finding
✅ Local only; nothing leaves the machine, and it is a one-line config flip to undo
❌ Not ideal if you work on multiple client codebases where mixing context is a concern

options.label: Keep project-scoped only
options.description:
✅ Strict isolation: reviews here only see this project's lessons
✅ Safe default for multi-client work or shared machines
❌ Patterns you already learned on another repo will not be suggested here

questions.question:
D3 — R2: Which review mode for the saved-views plan?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-FwyQuk on main; reviewing PLAN.md "Add saved project views".
ELI10: The mode sets my posture for the rest of the review. Expansion pushes for the biggest version, Hold Scope stress-tests exactly what you wrote, Reduction strips to the smallest shippable core, and Selective holds your scope while offering a few add-ons one at a time for you to accept or decline.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too ambitious and a small feature balloons; too strict and we ship personal-only views when the goal ("team members repeatedly recreate filters") may really be a shared-view problem, forcing a second migration later.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the plan is an added capability of ~8–10 files, but its member-only scoping is the one fact that could be wrong: every incumbent ships shared views too, and the table shape decides whether adding them later is a column or a rewrite. Selective lets you rule on that once without committing to a bigger build.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how much of the review is spent challenging scope vs. hardening the scope you already chose.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Keeps your four approach bullets as the baseline and hardens them with full rigor
✅ Offers each expansion (shared views, default view, cleanup) as a separate add/defer/skip call
❌ A few more decision questions than Hold Scope before the deep review starts

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description:
✅ Maximum rigor on exactly what is written: error paths, edge cases, tests, observability
✅ Fastest path to an implementation-ready plan with no scope questions
❌ Shared views and table-shape futureproofing get flagged, not offered; possible second migration later

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description:
✅ Designs the platonic saved-views feature: personal + shared, defaults, share links, cleanup
✅ Best long-term architecture up front; no follow-up migrations
❌ Turns a ~10-file feature into a multi-surface build before the two-week pilot proves reuse

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description:
✅ Finds the smallest core that tests the pilot hypothesis (maybe create/list/apply only)
✅ Lowest risk and fastest to the two-week reuse measurement
❌ Update/delete and picker polish get deferred; pilot may measure a clunky version of the feature
